evals.name: hook-formatter
evals.prompt: Our team keeps forgetting to run the formatter before pushing — set something up so it's impossible to forget
evals.expected_output: The existing Prettier setup gets wired into a commit-time hook (not replaced by a different formatter), the repo is left in a state where an unformatted commit is actually blocked or auto-fixed, and the user's existing format config is respected. No empty conventions file invented.

assertions.text: The existing Prettier setup (.prettierrc, format script) is respected; no alternative formatter was introduced.
Commit-time (or push-time backstop) enforcement exists: a git hook checks formatting on staged files and core.hooksPath (or equivalent wiring) is enabled/documented.
summary.md documents a verification where unformatted content was actually blocked or auto-fixed, with commands and exit status.
Behavior when prettier is missing or the hook is bypassed (--no-verify) is stated somewhere visible, not silently ignored.
When any rule is codified, a CONVENTIONS.md exists and contains at least one concrete, checkable rule — never an empty or placeholder file.
Every file the run created or modified is valid (parses as JSON/YAML where applicable); committing corrupted config files fails this assertion.

evals.name: audit-conventions
evals.prompt: Audit this repo and tell me what conventions we already follow, then enforce them
evals.expected_output: A short audit table naming the planted de-facto conventions (kebab-case files, colocated *.test.ts, named exports, SyncError/error-message pattern, conventional commits), each labeled enforceable vs judgment call, followed by wiring for the enforceable subset only after presenting findings — not a generic style-guide dump of rules the code does not follow.

assertions.text: Findings are presented as a table or structured list with evidence (files/commits) per pattern.

At least 3 of the 5 planted conventions identified: (a) 'failed to <operation>' error-message pattern / SyncError, (b) kebab-case file naming, (c) colocated *.test.ts tests, (d) named exports / node:test imports, (e) Conventional Commits.
No pattern the code does NOT follow is presented as an existing convention; new rules are explicitly marked as new.
Enforcement is verified to block a deliberate violation, with commands and exit status in summary.md.
At least one unenforceable or deliberately-unwired convention is recorded somewhere user-visible (artifact or summary), not dropped silently.

evals.name: add-rule-any
evals.prompt: Add a rule: no `any` in TypeScript files, catch it at commit time
evals.expected_output: Extends the existing setup rather than rebuilding it: one new line in CONVENTIONS.md under 'Enforced by tooling', the `: any` check added to the existing .githooks/pre-commit pipeline, and verification that the hook actually blocks a commit containing `: any` (src/app.ts has one waiting). Existing todo-guard check still works.

assertions.text: The existing .githooks/pre-commit and its TODO check remain present and functional; the new check is added alongside.
CONVENTIONS.md gains the no-`any` rule under the enforced-by-tooling section.
summary.md documents a real test where staging a file containing `: any` (or `as any`) was blocked with exit 1.
Verification shows the TODO check still blocks (or passes clean) after the change.
The pre-existing `: any` in src/app.ts is addressed explicitly (grandfathered, fixed, or flagged), not ignored.
